name: Linux Fundamentals
description: Navigating and administering Linux systems from the command line, including files, permissions, processes and shell pipelines.

questions.question: Which command lists the files in a directory including hidden ones (names starting with a dot)?
questions.explanation: -a (all) includes dotfiles; -h is human-readable sizes, -t sorts by time and -s shows sizes.

questions.question: What does the pwd command print?
options: The absolute path of the current working directory
questions.explanation: pwd stands for print working directory.

questions.question: What permissions does chmod 750 file set?
options: Owner rw-, group r--, others r--
Owner rwx, group r-x, others no permissions
Owner rwx, group rwx, others r-x
Owner r-x, group r--, others none
questions.explanation: 7 = rwx, 5 = r-x, 0 = ---, applied to owner, group and others respectively.

questions.question: Which command shows a snapshot of all running processes on the system?
questions.explanation: ps aux lists every process with owner, CPU and memory usage; df/du report disk usage and free reports memory.

questions.question: What does cmd > out.txt 2>&1 do?
options: Appends stdout to out.txt and discards stderr
Redirects stdout to out.txt, then points stderr at the same place, so both go to out.txt
questions.explanation: Redirections are processed left to right: stdout goes to the file, then 2>&1 duplicates stderr onto stdout's current target.

questions.question: Which command finds all .log files under /var modified within the last 7 days?
questions.explanation: -mtime -7 means modified less than 7 days ago; +7 means more than 7 days ago. grep searches contents, not modification times.

practical.title: Top IPs from an access log
practical.instructions: Write one shell pipeline that prints the 5 most frequent IP addresses (the first space-separated field of each line) in access.log, along with how many times each appears.
practical.expected_output: awk '{print $1}' access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -5 (or cut -d' ' -f1 in place of awk).

rubric.hint: Use awk '{print $1}' or cut -d' ' -f1 to get the IP column.
uniq only collapses adjacent duplicates, so sort first.
uniq -c prefixes each line with its count.
Use sort -rn to put the highest counts first.

tasks.title: Complete Linux Journey: Command Line and Text-Fu
tasks.description: Work through the Getting Started, Command Line and Text-Fu sections of Linux Journey in a real terminal (WSL, a VM or a Linux machine).
tasks.completion_criteria: You can navigate directories, create/move/delete files and use pipes and redirection without notes.

tasks.title: Play OverTheWire Bandit levels 0-10
tasks.description: Solve the first 10 Bandit levels, which practise ssh, file reading, find, grep and permissions. Write down the command that solved each level.
tasks.completion_criteria: Levels 0-10 solved with a notes file of commands used.

tasks.title: Manage users, permissions and processes
tasks.description: On a VM, create users and groups, set file permissions with chmod/chown, manage services with systemctl, and inspect processes with ps, top and kill. Read the Linux Journey sections on permissions, processes and init.
tasks.completion_criteria: A shared directory writable only by one group, and a service you started, stopped and enabled at boot.

tasks.title: Write a system health-check script
tasks.description: Write a Bash script that reports disk, memory, CPU load, failed services and the top log errors, with arguments and error handling. Schedule it with cron and save its output to a dated log file.
tasks.completion_criteria: Script runs via cron, handles missing tools gracefully and produces a readable report.
